All walkthroughs / Health organisation

Health organisation · Cardiology

Build a pipeline version on a development sample of locked recordings

A data engineer has written a pipeline version that is still in development, so it may run only on development data. The engineer asks for a sample of the locked recordings, a custodian who did not ask approves fewer, and the platform draws them without anybody choosing. The pipeline version then runs for real on the sample and is refused on the real recordings. The sample ends, and recordings that hold no real person are declared synthetic.

11Steps
2People
about 9Minutes to read
Who is involved
Devi
Data engineer in the Health organisation
Hartley
Data custodian and approver for the Cardiology department

How to read this page

  • Every step is one screen, or one moment, in a real run. The label under the title names where it happens, and the step reads in the same order each time: what is happening, the evidence, and then what to look for in it.
  • Screenshots are real pictures of the Munitas console, the web app that people open in a browser. Click any picture to enlarge it.
  • Every name of a person, patient or card holder in the example data is invented, and every screenshot is unedited apart from being cropped to the part that matters.

Words used on this page

Organisation
A company or hospital group that uses Munitas. Each organisation sees only its own data.
Department
A team inside an organisation that owns some of its data, such as Cardiology.
Dataset
A named collection of records, such as a table of patient admissions.
Custodian
A person who holds the data custodian role, which allows deciding who may read data. A custodian decides for the departments they are an approver for.
Department approver
A custodian who is listed for one department and may approve access to its data and confirm claims about it. A department can have several, and any one of them can act on their own.
Sealed
Finished and closed for good, so that it can never be edited.
Version
One sealed state of a dataset. Changing the contents means making a new version, never editing an old one.
Pipeline
A series of steps that Munitas runs on a dataset version, each step after the ones it depends on. The last step is a gate decision.
Run
One execution of an agent or a pipeline, started for a stated purpose.
Custom step
A step of a pipeline whose script was written by the person who registered the pipeline, instead of one of the steps Munitas provides. It runs in a closed container with no internet, no key and no storage address, and can only ask the platform for the recordings it is allowed to read and send back the files it makes.
Stage
Where a version of a pipeline is in its life. In development means the version runs only on development data, which is a small sample or recordings with no real person in them. In production means it runs on any data the department allows. Retired means it has ended for good and cannot be run again.
Development sample
A few recordings drawn by the platform from a sealed version of locked recordings, for building and testing a pipeline version that is still in development. It names the same locked recordings as the original and copies none, and it ends on its own.
Locked recording
A recording stored scrambled under a key made for the one patient it is about. Reading it back needs the platform to open it, and destroying the patient’s key later makes it unreadable for good.
Synthetic
Made up, with no real person in it, such as sentences read aloud by volunteers from invented scripts.

PART ONE

Devi asks for a sample of the recordings

A pipeline is a series of steps that Munitas runs on a version of a dataset. A pipeline version that has a custom step, a step whose script was written by the person who registered the pipeline, starts in development, which means it may run only on development data. For recordings of patients, development data is a small sample of them, or recordings that hold no real person. This part shows where a sample comes from.

1
Devi
Devi asks for a development sample of the recordings
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Devi is a data engineer in the Cardiology department of the Health organisation. A department is the team inside an organisation that owns some of its data. Devi has written a pipeline version whose step makes the first half second of each recording silent, and it is in development. Devi opens the sealed version of the consultation recordings, which means the version that is finished and closed for good, so that it can never be edited. Under the heading Development samples, Devi says how many recordings are wanted, for how many days, and what the sample is for. Devi cannot choose which recordings: the platform draws them.

The heading Development samples explains that a sample is a few of these recordings, drawn by the platform, that names the same locked recordings and copies none. Under Ask for a sample, Draw a sample for me. is selected, the boxes read 4 recordings and 5 days, and the purpose reads Building a step that makes the first half second of each recording silent. The limits are written beside the boxes: at most 50 recordings and at most 14 days.
2
Devi
The request waits for an approver
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Pressing the button records the request and does nothing else. A sample needs the agreement of an approver of the department that owns the recordings, and the approver cannot be the person asking. An approver is a data custodian, a person who may decide who reads a department’s data, who is listed for that department. Devi may withdraw the request while it waits.

Under Your samples a row reads Waiting for an approver and Asked for 4 recordings for 5 days, to build and test with, and offers the button Withdraw this request. The form above now offers only Name the recordings that went wrong., because a request to draw a sample is already waiting.
3
Hartley
Hartley sees the request, and cannot choose the recordings
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Hartley is the data custodian for Cardiology, so the same page shows the request to Hartley, under Waiting for your decision. It says who asked, how many recordings, for how many days and why. Hartley may lower the number or the days, and may not raise them. Hartley may not pick recordings either: the platform draws them, so nobody can steer a sample towards particular patients.

Under Waiting for your decision a yellow box reads Devi asks for 4 recordings for 5 days, to build and test with., then the purpose. Two boxes, Recordings and Days, each say that you may lower this, and a third reads A note, recorded with your decision. The text says You cannot choose the recordings: the platform draws them. The buttons are Approve and Decline. A white box above them lets an approver declare recordings synthetic, which step 10 uses.
4
Hartley
Hartley approves fewer recordings, and the platform draws them
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Hartley lowers the request to 3 recordings for 3 days, adds a note, and approves. The platform then draws the recordings by one fixed method: at most one recording from each patient, spread across short, medium and long recordings, and picked by a value that comes out the same every time for the same person asking for the same purpose. Nobody chooses, including Hartley. The platform seals a new version, the sample, that names the same locked recordings as the original. No audio is copied.

Under In force for these recordings one line reads Devi: 3 recordings (1 short, 1 medium and 1 long), ends followed by a date three days away, and offers End this sample. The line shows how many recordings came from each length and names nobody but Devi: no recording and no patient.
PART TWO

Devi uses the sample

Devi now runs the pipeline version on the sample. Running it on the real recordings is still refused, which shows what development means.

5
Devi
Devi opens the sample, which says what it is
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

The platform made the sample as a version of its own, in a dataset named after the recordings with dev-sample and a short code added. A dataset is a registered, owned collection of data. Devi opens the sample from the list of Devi’s own samples. The page counts 3 recordings of 3 patients and says that the sample is for the person it was drawn for and for nobody else. Lower down, the section Where this came from names the platform’s own step that made the sample, and links to the recordings it was made from.

Under Locked recordings the counts read Recordings 3 and Patients 3. Under Development sample a green box reads This is a development sample of 3 recordings, drawn for you., then the date it ends, and says that it names the same locked recordings as the recordings it was drawn from and copies none of them. Under Where this came from, Step reads development_sample, Code version reads sample:v1 and Environment reads platform.
6
Devi
On the real recordings the same pipeline version is refused
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Devi opens the real recordings again, chooses the pipeline version and presses Start. The platform refuses before it starts anything. A pipeline version in development may run only on development data, and the real recordings are not development data for anybody. Nothing is left behind: no run, no file and no record of an attempt to read.

A red box reads Nothing was started. Fix these first: and says that this version is in development, so it can be run only on development data: recordings declared synthetic, or a development sample drawn for you. It names the custom step silence, says that on any other data an approver of the department that owns the pipeline has to check the version and move it to production first, and ends Ask for a sample on the page of the recordings.
7
Devi
On the sample the pipeline version runs for real
Munitas console · Pipeline run · /pipeline-runs/<id>

Devi opens the sample, chooses the same pipeline version and presses Start, and this time it runs. The script runs in a container, which is an isolated environment. This one has no internet and holds no key and no storage address. It asks the platform for its recordings and is told of exactly the 3 in the sample. The platform finds the stored files that the sample names, unlocks each with its own patient’s key inside the platform, and hands the sound over. What the step writes back becomes a new version that waits for a person’s review.

The heading reads Running, the name of the pipeline, against, and the name of the recordings followed by dev-sample and a short code. The page says Finished. Under Steps, silence reads Done and has a link Open the version it made, and decide also reads Done.
PART THREE

The sample ends

A sample ends when its days are over, or sooner when the person it was drawn for, or an approver, ends it. Nothing is left running on it afterwards.

8
Devi
Devi ends the sample when the work is done
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Devi presses End this sample on the page of the real recordings. The row changes to Ended, and the form for asking appears again with Draw a sample for me selected, because the earlier request is over and a new one may be made.

Under Your samples the row reads Ended and 3 recordings, to build and test with, and has no buttons. The form above offers both kinds of sample again, with Draw a sample for me. selected.
9
Devi
A run on an ended sample is refused
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Devi opens the ended sample and tries to run the pipeline version on it. The platform refuses at the start, for the same reason as on the real recordings: the sample is no longer development data for Devi. A step that is already running when a sample ends is refused at its next request.

A red box reads Nothing was started. Fix these first: and gives the same reason as before, that the version is in development and can be run only on development data.
PART FOUR

Recordings that hold no real person

Some recordings hold no real person, for example sentences read aloud by volunteers from invented scripts. They need no sample.

10
Hartley
Hartley declares a version of recordings synthetic
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

Synthetic means made up, with no real person in it. An approver of the owning department may declare a version of recordings synthetic, and must give a reason. Hartley opens a version of recordings that volunteers read aloud and types why.

Under Development samples a white box reads If these recordings hold no real person, declare them synthetic. Then any pipeline version in development may run on them, and nobody needs a sample. The reason box reads Read aloud by volunteers from invented scripts, so no patient is in them, beside the button Declare these recordings synthetic.
11
Hartley
The declaration is recorded, with who made it and why
Munitas console · Version detail · /versions/<id>

After Hartley presses the button, the page says who made the declaration, when, and why. From then on a pipeline version in development may run on these recordings for anybody in the organisation, because nobody real is in them. A development sample holds real recordings, so it can never be declared synthetic.

A green box has three lines. Declared synthetic by Hartley on a date and time. Reason given: Read aloud by volunteers from invented scripts, so no patient is in them. No real person is in these recordings, so a pipeline version in development may run on them.

What the platform refuses and draws is proved separately by verify/v142_development_samples.py, and the whole loop on a real step by verify/v143_development_loop.py. Every person, patient and card holder in the example data is invented.
